records.before_content:
add_memory's `entities` parameter takes STRUCTURED REFERENTS, not labels, and a second guard then checks them against the content. Two rejections hit in sequence on 2026-09-21:

1. `entities=["Task 4131", "Task 3764", ...]` is rejected with error_type ValidationError: "each declared referent must be a dict of the shape {'kind': 'task', 'id': <digits>, 'project_id': <optional>}"; 'kind' and 'project_id' are optional and default to 'task' and the local project, but 'id' must be the digits (int or ASCII-digit string), "never a label like \"Task 3127\"".

2. With the shape fixed, the call was then rejected with error_type DeclaredReferentConflictRejected / `declared_referent_conflict`. The response names `declared`, `conflicts` and `content_referents`, i.e. it tells you exactly which declared referent your own content does not actually discuss. In this case task 5550 was declared but appeared in the content only as "task 5739 (depends on 5550)" — a mention, not a subject. Dropping it succeeded.

The guard's own hint is the operating rule: it "rejects only a CONFLICT, never an absence — omitting `entities`, or passing [] to record that you considered referents and none applied, always succeeds." So when in doubt, omit `entities` and let the content scan derive the set; declaring is worth it only when you are confident every id you name is something the content is genuinely ABOUT.

Also observed: a decisions_and_rationale write routes to graphiti and returns `memory_ids: []` with `stores_written: ["graphiti"]` and "Memory queued" — an empty id list there is normal, not a failure.
records.rationale: Quotes the gate hint and concludes "when in doubt, omit `entities`".

records.before_content: add_memory entities-declaration gotcha (observed 2026-09-27). add_memory rejects with DeclaredReferentConflictRejected when the declared `entities` name tasks that the content scan does not find in the text. The scan recognised "task 185", "task 173's" and "task 184's" as task referents. It did NOT recognise a task number embedded in a topic slug ("task-173-liveness-investigation") or written as "gate 184". So declaring Task 173/184 on such content was rejected even though the memory is about them. Fix: either write the plain "task N" form in the text, or omit `entities` (or pass []), which always succeeds and lets the scan derive referents. The rejection writes nothing, so it is safe to retry.
records.rationale: Fix clause: "or omit `entities` (or pass []), which always succeeds".

records.before_content: Root cause of the false DeclaredReferentConflictRejected rejections (found 2026-09-28, owner task 6059): fused_memory/utils/referent_resolution.py::_conflicting_referents applies the rule 'the scanner's silence is uninformative' per KIND, not per REFERENT. A declared task conflicts iff the scan found ANY task of that kind and not this one. So 'Merged task-173-fillet-fix; closes the loop.' with declared 173 is ACCEPTED (empty scan), but 'Merged task-173-fillet-fix after task 170 landed.' with declared 173 is REJECTED, although the scanner's inability to see the slug is identical in both. Reproduced directly through entities_gate with group_id reify for slug (task-173-foo), branch name (task/173), non-task vocabulary (gate 184) and list forms (Tasks 5949/5849, tasks 3659 and 3500). The PRD's adjacent-number typo catch ([3127, 3129] against 'Task 3127', pinned by tests/test_referent_resolution.py::test_a_superset_conflicts_per_ref) and the blind-spot tolerance (pinned only for the EMPTY-scan case by test_the_scanners_blind_list_never_manufactures_a_conflict) collide in the mixed case, which no test exercised, and the rule resolves every mixed case as a typo.
records.rationale: States the root cause in _conflicting_referents correctly.

records.before_content: Two compounding facts about add_memory's entities gate (2026-09-28, task 6059): (1) on a Mem0-primary category (observations_and_summaries, procedural_knowledge, preferences_and_norms) with dual_write=False the declaration is validated against the content and then DISCARDED — the add_memory docstring's own scope note says so — so on those writes the gate can only ever cost a false rejection and never buys attribution; the solar_challenge_platform sighting was exactly that category. (2) entities_gate.py::_ENTITIES_CONFLICT_HINT tells the rejected agent to 'drop entities entirely'; agents obeyed and recorded 'omitting entities fixes it' as durable memories (solar_challenge_platform 4214c151-8776-4efa-99dd-8a12f02906e1 by curator-scp-185-rollup-split-2026-09-27; dark_factory 525ad930, 454d5a87, d3d753ef), which teach every future agent to stop declaring — against PRD plans/memory-referent-fidelity-prd.md decision 4, whose adoption census is task 3676. On a Graphiti-primary write, dropping the declaration also misattributes the memory to whichever task the scanner could see.
records.rationale: Names the omission advice as the harm; correct.

records.before_content: Convention (task 3675): every in-repo site that teaches add_memory/add_episode referent declaration is certified by fused-memory/tests/test_referent_declaration_examples.py. Its _GUARDED_SITES tuple lists them. Each `entities=<list literal>` is EXECUTED against the live entities_gate together with the content= string of its own call. The extractor fails loudly on placeholders (`entities=[<id>]`), on non-literals, and on prose `entities=` with no list after it, so write "omit `entities`" without the "=". Every guarded site must show at least one NON-EMPTY declaration whose content names the task it declares, because [] alone teaches nothing about the entry shape. A new site is one more _GUARDED_SITES entry: import Python constants, never regex their source. If it is a skills/ file, also register it in SKILLS_CONSUMING_TESTS and in the dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml enumeration. The recon prompts get the text from fused_memory.utils.referent_resolution::render_referent_declaration_guidance, which composes _DECLARED_REFERENT_HINT. Do not restate the entry shape anywhere else.
records.rationale: Declaration-examples convention; its "omit `entities`" is about how to spell prose for the extractor, not advice to omit.

records.before_content: Gotcha when a Mem0 memory in one project cites a dark_factory task (measured 2026-09-29 with fused_memory.utils.referent_resolution.resolve_referents, default registry). In a solar_challenge_platform memory, the bare form "task 6059" is scanned as the LOCAL project's task 6059, which misattributes the memory. Writing both "dark_factory task 6059" and "dark_factory:6059" makes 6059 AMBIGUOUS. Only the qualified form "dark_factory:6059", used alone, resolves to project_id='dark_factory'. A placeholder such as "task NNN" derives no referent. So cite cross-project tasks ONLY as <project_id>:<id>, and never also as the word form "task <id>".
records.rationale: Cross-project citation gotcha for the referent scanner; correct.
